about.title: Daly City Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Few people in Daly City think about who made the space heater in the hallway, the tires on the car, or the ladder in the garage — until something fails. When a product breaks in a way it never should, California law treats it differently from an ordinary accident. Under strict liability, you generally do not need to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show the product had a defect — in its design, in how that unit was built, or in its warnings — and that the defect caused your injury. That path can reach the maker, the distributor, and the retailer who sold it. Product failures happen on the road, too. Of the 257 injury collisions recorded in Daly City in 2025, some on I-280 or Mission Street may trace back to a component that gave out rather than a driver's choice. Whatever the product, keep it. Do not repair, return, or discard it. LawProactive is a free service connecting San Mateo County residents with an independent attorney who takes these claims on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Daly City Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict liability changes the question
items.desc: In many California product cases you do not have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. An attorney who works these claims knows how to frame a design, manufacturing, or warning defect from the start.

items.title: The product itself is the evidence
items.desc: A defective item that gets repaired, returned to a store, or tossed in the bin can take the claim with it. The attorneys we connect you with will tell you how to preserve the product, its packaging, and receipts before anyone else handles it.

items.title: More than one company may answer for it
items.desc: California allows claims against the manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer in the chain of sale. Identifying every responsible party matters, and it is work you should not have to do alone while recovering.

items.question: My airbag did not deploy in a crash on John Daly Boulevard. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. The crash itself may involve another driver, while the airbag failure may be a separate manufacturing or design defect claim against the vehicle or component maker. Keep the car from being scrapped or repaired until an attorney has had a chance to look at it, because the module and the sensors are the proof. An attorney in the LawProactive network can sort out which claims apply and who should be named.

items.question: Do I need to show the company was careless?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product had a defect in its design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the maker tried hard to be careful is not the central issue. That said, each case turns on its own facts, and an attorney can tell you how the rule fits yours.

items.question: The store in Daly City offered me a refund if I return the item. Should I take it?
items.answer: Talk to an attorney before handing anything over. Returning the product means giving up the single most important piece of evidence, and a refund is not compensation for an injury. Photograph it, store it safely, and keep the receipt and packaging. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who will advise you on next steps at no cost to you.
